stemMd: A small uncharged lipid-soluble molecule crosses a cell membrane even after membrane transport proteins are inhibited. What mechanism best explains this?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Passage through nuclear pores in the plasma membrane

options.label: E
options.textMd: Simple diffusion through the lipid bilayer

explanationMd: The hydrophobic interior of the lipid bilayer permits many small nonpolar or lipid-soluble molecules to dissolve in it and diffuse across. Net movement follows the concentration gradient and does not need a transporter or ATP. Charge and low lipid solubility would make direct passage less favourable.

distractorRationale.b: This requires membrane proteins and vesicle formation.
distractorRationale.c: The observation does not require an active pump.
distractorRationale.d: Translation produces proteins rather than transporting this molecule.
distractorRationale.a: Nuclear pores belong to the nuclear envelope, not the plasma membrane.
